analysis:
Examined both supplied release-provider.yml excerpts (head lines 1–1068) against the complete changed-range map and canonical definition index; only selected threat definitions had full detail. The executable change at lines 829–834 strengthens final extracted-app verification by requiring Apple's anchor, provider identifier and team identity in addition to deep/strict signature validation. No supported security regression was identified in that change. Other changes in these units document dev-branch routing and signing, rather than implement those policies.
Relevant contracts are release-key authority (A-005), binary registry integrity (A-011), durable build qualifications (A-017/T-054), operator code tampering (T-013/T-034), and privileged helper identity (TB-010/T-044). Surrounding checks retain helper-specific signing, profile/entitlement validation, notarization, archive-to-app byte comparisons, full CodeDirectory measurement and publication digest outputs. Nothing supplied changes inference plaintext handling, cache isolation (T-041), billing or serving authorization directly; successful signing must not be treated as authorization or independent qualification.
Integration must verify scripts/provider-release-resume.py verify-source, invoked at lines 138–146, and resolve-provider-release.sh at lines 151–164 together with both caller workflows: the newly documented dev-source admission must remain dev-only, with prod secrets unavailable to that lane. Since every environment shares the signing team and identifier (lines 21–24), also reconcile that policy with publication provenance and updater environment selection before concluding dev artifacts cannot enter production. These implementations and the remainder of staging/publication beyond line 1068 are not supplied here; their absence is a coverage limit, not evidence of a missing control.
